div.head: SUBSECT. 7.
Sleeping and waking, causes.
div.p:
What I have formerly said of Exercise, I may now repeat of Sleep. Nothing better than moderate sleep, nothing worse than it, if it be in extremes, or unseasonably used. It is a received opinion, that a melancholy man cannot sleep overmuch; Somnus supra modum prodest [additional sleep is beneficial], as an only
Antidote, and nothing offends them more, or causeth this malady sooner, than waking, yet in some cases sleep may do more harm than good in that phlegmatic, swinish, cold, and sluggish melancholy, which Melanchthon speaks of, that thinks of waters, sighing most part, &c. Path. lib. 1 cap. 17 Fernel.It dulls the Spirits, if overmuch, and senses, fills the head full of gross humours, causeth distillations, rheums, great store of excrements in the brain, and all the other parts, as Lib. 2 sect. 2 cap. 4.Fuchsius speaks of them, that sleep like so many Dormice. Or if it be used in the daytime, upon a full stomach, the body ill composed to rest, or after hard meats, it increaseth fearful dreams, Incubus, night-walking, crying out, & much unquietness; such sleep prepares the body, as Jo. Katzschius lib. de rebus 6 non naturalibus.one observes, to many perilous diseases. But as I have said, waking overmuch, is both a symptom, and an ordinary cause. It causeth dryness of the brain, frenzy, dotage, & makes the body dry, lean, hard, and ugly to behold, as Instit. ad vitam optimam cap. 26.Lemnius hath it. The temperature of the Brain is corrupted by it, the humours adust, the eyes made to sink into the head, choler increased, and the whole body inflamed: and, as may be added out of Galen 3 de sanitate tuenda, Avicenna 3. 1, Attenuant juvenum vigilatae corpora noctes [Wakeful nights enfeeble the bodies of young men].it overthrows the natural heat, it causeth crudities, hurts concoction, and what not? Not without good cause therefore Crato consil. 21 lib. 2, Hildesheim spicil. 2 de delir. & Mania, Jacchinus, Arculanus on Rhasis, Guainerius and Mercurialis, reckon up this overmuch waking, as a principal cause.
